problem: Find the value of $c$ that satisfies the mean value theorem for $f(x)={log}_{3}⁡x$ on the interval $[9,81].$
worked_solution:
The function $f(x)$ is continuous on $[9,81]$ and differentiable on $(9,81),$ hence, we can apply the Mean Value Theorem. 

So, the mean value theorem states that there exists a $c\in (9,81)$ such that

$$
{f}^{′}(c)=\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}.
$$

Plugging in $a=9$ and $b=81$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(c) & =\frac{f(81)-f(9)}{81-9} \\  & =\frac{{log}_{3}⁡(81)-{log}_{3}⁡(9)}{72} \\  & =\frac{4-2}{72} \\  & =\frac{1}{36}.\end{aligned}
$$

Differentiating the function, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({log}_{3}⁡x)=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{f}^{′}(c)=\frac{1}{c\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.
$$

Finally, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{c\operatorname{ln}⁡3} & =\frac{1}{36} \\ c & =\frac{36}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.\end{aligned}
$$
